parts.part: Long-form type: headings, lists, quotes, code

leaves.what: src/components/prose.tsx: Prose (the column), H2, H3, P, UL, OL, LI, Quote (figure + blockquote + figcaption), Code, Kbd, Note, each a type primitive drawn as the element the document needs, with list markers, the quote's bar and the spacing written by hand.
leaves.why: The kit has type primitives and no prose component: nothing lays out running text, a list, a quotation or code.

leaves.what: Read primitives/Typography.tsx past the doc comments to find that `blockquote` is in `TextElement`.
leaves.why: Every doc comment lists 'a heading, `p`, `span`, `div`, `label`, `li`, `dt`, `dd`, `legend`, `figcaption` among them': blockquote, strong, em, time are in the union and not named.

leaves.what: `font-mono` on inline code, kbd and the code blocks.
leaves.why: Skill: "`font-mono` is the project's mono face ... write it where the project wants one (an identifier, a time, an amount). No kit component uses it."

leaves.what: The h1 is `<Headline size="medium" className="md:text-display-small md:font-display-small">`.
leaves.why: Display's doc comment: "`size` is the size on the narrowest screen; name a larger one from a breakpoint with the two utilities a role is made of, its text and its font".

leaves.what: Headings take `tabIndex={-1}` and `focusRing({ className })`, so the table of contents can move the focus to them.
leaves.why: Skill: "The ring is `focusRing` from `<kit>/utils.ts`; extend it, do not invent another."

leaves.what: `max-w-prose` (Tailwind's 65ch) as the measure of the text column.
leaves.why: The kit has no token or utility for a line length of running text.

parts.notes: Type-checked and rendered to a string, not seen in a browser. Emphasis inside a paragraph is a plain <strong>, at the browser's weight. A block of code has no syntax colours (no highlighter in the project, and no colour roles for one).

parts.part: A table of contents that follows the scroll

leaves.what: src/components/TableOfContents.tsx: `useActiveSection`, a scroll and resize listener (one read a frame) that takes the last heading above a line 112px under the top of the window, and the last heading of all at the page's end; and the list of links that marks it (`aria-current="location"`, a bar at its start, the primary colour).
leaves.why: The kit has no table of contents, no anchor navigation and nothing that follows the scroll.

leaves.what: Wide (lg): a `nav` that sticks beside the text. Narrow: a bar that sticks to the top, names the section being read and opens the list. One of the two is `display: none` at any width.
leaves.why: Expected of a screen.

leaves.what: The phone's bar is the kit's `Disclosure`, controlled, with its panel taken out of the flow by `className="absolute inset-x-0 top-full ..."` on `DisclosurePanel` and `relative` on the root; closing on Escape (focus back to the trigger, found by its `data-slot`), on a press outside, on the focus leaving the bar and on a link followed is written by hand around it.
leaves.why: A Disclosure's panel pushes the page down: opened in a bar that sticks, closing it after a link is followed would move the text under the reader. The kit has no disclosure that lays its panel over the page, and `Popover`/`Menu` would make the list a dialog or a menu instead of a `nav` of links.

leaves.what: Read Disclosure.tsx past its doc comments: that `className` reaches the panel's root (the element that carries the height), that the root is `group/disclosure` with `data-expanded`, and the trigger's `data-slot`.
leaves.why: The doc comment names `contentClassName` and `isUnstyled`, and not what `className` styles, nor the group name the chevron itself keys on.

leaves.what: The link of the section being read is drawn by `className` on the kit's `Link`: `border-s-4 border-primary text-primary`, against `border-transparent`.
leaves.why: `Link` takes `aria-current` and has no look for it; `color` is `primary` or `inherit` and there is no selected or current state.

leaves.what: `aria-current` and `onPress` on `Link`; `onPress` moves the focus to the heading (`focus({ preventScroll: true })`) while the adapter scrolls to the fragment.
leaves.why: Link's doc comment: "It takes React Aria's `Link` props (`href`, `target`, `rel`, `download`, `routerOptions`, `onPress`, `isDisabled`, `aria-current`)". The adapter's: "The focus is not moved: move it yourself where the target should take it."

leaves.what: Two type primitives (`Label` "On this page" over a `Title` with the section's name, each `block`) are put inside `DisclosureTrigger`'s children, which the trigger wraps in its own `title-medium` span.
leaves.why: The trigger has one label and a `trailing` slot, no supporting line under the label; the classes of the inner primitives win over the span's.

parts.notes: NOT RUN IN A BROWSER: no browser tool was allowed. The scroll-following, the fragment scroll through the router adapter, the focus move, the overlay panel of the bar and its closing were type-checked and rendered to a string (the links' hrefs, `aria-current`, the panel's classes are in the markup), never scrolled or pressed. Unsure: whether the absolute panel's height transition and `hidden` behave as in the flow; whether the heading's `scroll-mt-24` clears the bar exactly on a phone. Following a link drops `?dark` from the address (the class stays on <html>). Known limit: at the page's end the last entry is the one marked, so a link followed to a late section that cannot reach the top of the window marks the last entry, not the one pressed.

parts.notes: NOT RUN IN A BROWSER: playing, seeking, the speed, the volume, the caption timing and the error path are type-checked and rendered to a string only; none was heard or pressed. THE RECORDING IS A MOCK: there is no speech synthesis on this machine, so public/audio/send-your-first-invoice.mp3 (45 s, generated with node and ffmpeg) is eight soft tones, one a caption, at the cues' times; the captions hold the words a narration would say. The captions are drawn from the cue data in the client, not from a WebVTT `<track>` (a browser draws no cues for an <audio> element, so the page must draw them either way; a real one would parse the .vtt). The caption box is not a live region, on purpose. The seek slider's keyboard step is one second. The mock file was made with node and ffmpeg (a temporary .wav, removed).

friction: The build was green at the first `npm run build`: no prop was guessed wrong, but only because I read sources. What was hard: (1) Props are often not in the doc comment. IconButton's `icon`, the required `aria-label`, the default variant and a toggle's `isSelected`/`onChange` are only in the types; Slider's props sit in an uncommented interface; EmptyState and Menu name behaviours, not every prop. A one-line usage example with the props, as Tabs and Breadcrumbs have, would have saved each read. (2) The type primitives' comments list ten elements 'among them' while the union has more (blockquote, time, strong, em): an article needs exactly those. (3) Long-form writing has nothing: no prose rhythm, no measure token, no code block, no inline code, no list or quote style. The skill could say so in one line and name `font-mono` and a surface tier for code. (4) `Tag` is the static one and the thing a site calls a tag is a `Chip` with `href`: clear once both doc comments are read, not from the names. (5) Nothing in the kit is a pressable container: `Card` refuses, `ListItem` is read unless in a grid list, `Link` is text. A previous/next link, a transcript row, a result card all need a raw React Aria `Link`/`Button` plus `StateLayer` and `focusRing`; a documented recipe (or a `Pressable` surface) would make that one obvious step. (6) `Link` takes `aria-current` and has no look for it; any navigation list (a table of contents, a side menu of a doc site) needs one. (7) `Disclosure` cannot lay its panel over the page; I reached around with `absolute` on the panel after reading where `className` lands. (8) `Slider` cannot show or speak a value that is not a number (a time). (9) Material's primary/secondary tabs rule does not say what two sets of tabs in running text should be. (10) `npx shadcn@latest add @ds/site-header-block -y` was refused by this session's permissions (the command was denied before it ran), so the block was copied from kit-blocks/ as the brief allows. (11) With no browser I could not see any of it: the skill has nothing for checking a screen without one, so scroll-following, playback and captions are unverified beyond types and a server render.
